name: KeyLab mkII
//: The names these report themselves by. The device on this desk calls its ALSA client `KeyLab mkII 49`, which is the model rather than the family, so both patterns are kept.
//identity: Read off the device on 2026-08-29 with a universal identity request: F0 7E 7F 06 02 00 20 6B 02 00 05 62 54 01 03 01 F7. Firmware 1.3.1.84.
//ports: Two, not the three that were guessed here before. There is no separate MCU port and no DIN port: the second one is called DAW and carries whichever DAW protocol the DAW Map setting names.

ports.note: notes, pads, encoders, faders, the select buttons and the wheels
the DAW protocol chosen by Global Settings, DAW Map. Mackie Control when that reads Default MCU, and something else entirely for every other choice

//screen: Arturia's own text, the same protocol and address a MiniLab 3's screen takes: write a string to preset 02, param 60, control 01. On the DAW port, not the main one, settled by writing to each on its own. Three things about it cost an afternoon. It renders the first chunk and ignores the second, and a message with the second chunk trimmed off renders nothing at all, so it is sent whole. It must not be sent the switching-on message a MiniLab needs first: sent that, it takes nothing afterwards. And it is not ready the instant it appears on the bus, so the greeting is said again a few seconds after the application starts, which is the difference between the same bytes working by hand and doing nothing at startup. Reading the address answers 7F, so the field is write-only the way the MiniLab's Selected Preset Name is, and it was found by writing to it. What it will not take at all is Mackie display text, refused on four model bytes and both ports while the device was provably speaking Mackie Control in Standard MCU.
//controls: What every User preset and every bank agree on. The pads are not here because they send notes rather than controllers and this file describes controllers; they are in the note below.
//programs: The banks, which is what a program is on this device. All ten User presets carry these same numbers, so a preset is not a program here: only the bank changes what arrives.

programs.name: User bank 1
programs.//: Arturia's own Analog Lab assignments, and the first eight knobs are the eight a MiniLab 3 sends in its Arturia program. Read back as Relative 1 with acceleration 1:1, so these count notches rather than reporting a position.

programs.name: User bank 2 or 3
programs.//: One entry for two banks, because the two are identical from the factory: bank 3 answers with the same numbers bank 2 does, and only the names differ (Encoder 1B2 against Encoder 1B3), which is how the reading was checked. Written as one program rather than two, since two programs sharing every number would leave neither able to be told from the other. Absolute here, unlike bank 1, so an endless encoder is reporting a position and has to be read as movement.

note:
49 keys, nine endless encoders, nine faders, nine RGB select buttons under them, sixteen pads, a DAW command section of ten buttons, transport, four CV outputs and a screen with a clickable centre knob. Three modes, chosen by the three buttons under that knob: Analog Lab, DAW and User. Everything in this file is what it sends in User mode, and that is the whole of what can be described here.

Read off the device on 2026-08-29 through Arturia's own settings protocol, the same one sysex-controls speaks, and checked page by page against sysex-controls itself on screen. Firmware 1.3.1, model KeyLab mkII 49. Nothing was written to the device and no preset was recalled or stored.

All ten User presets hold the same controller numbers. Only their names differ, and only one has been named: User 1 is Reason, User 2 to 10 are DEFAULT 2 to DEFAULT 10. So a User preset is not a program as far as this file is concerned, and the bank is: bank 1 is Arturia's Analog Lab layout counting notches, banks 2 and 3 are a plain absolute layout and are identical to each other.

Every control reads its channel as User, meaning it follows the global User MIDI channel rather than naming one of its own. That channel currently reads 1. So no channel is claimed here.

The pads are sixteen notes on channel 10, gated, and they are the one thing that differs between presets: User 1 runs 36 to 51 straight up, and User 2 to 10 have the rows the other way about, starting 48 49 50 51 on the top row and ending 36 37 38 39 on the bottom. Notes rather than controllers, so they cannot be written into the lists above.

The pitch bend wheel sends pitch bend on the keyboard channel and has no controller number at all; its page on the device offers a channel and a range and nothing else. The mod wheel is CC 1 and is in the list.

What this file cannot describe is DAW mode. There the front panel is hard mapped and the numbers come from whichever DAW the Global Settings DAW Map names: Default MCU, Default HUI, Live, Logic, Protools, Cubase, Studio One, Reaper or MMC. The manual is candid that a DAW not on the list is probably fine on MCU or HUI. The device read DAW Map = Live on 2026-08-29, which is Ableton's protocol and is not something JingleBox2 reads. Set it to Default MCU and this application has the whole surface today, faders, encoders, mute, solo, banking, the display and the button lights, through Midi/MidiMackieRouter.cs and Midi/MackieSurface.cs. Its faders offer Pickup or Jump, which are this application's Takeover and Jump under other names, and both currently read Pickup.

Other globals as read: pads backlight off, low power on, octave button blink on, DAW buttons DAW rather than User, track control buttons Single Track, MIDI in to USB and USB to MIDI out both on.

Sources: the device itself, docs/keylab-mkii_Manual_2_2_0_EN.pdf for the panel names, and github.com/soyersoyer/sysex-controls for the protocol and the control ids.
